style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On May&#160;1, 2026, we committed to a plan to cease operations at our Cabo, Brazil manufacturing facility as of June&#160;30, 2026. We expect to incur pre-tax non-recurring charges of approximately $43 million under the plan, of which approximately $36 million is expected to consist of impairment charges relating to fixed assets and inventory write-downs and approximately $7 million is expected to consist of cash expenditures for employee-related costs, severance payments, and other termination-related costs. We expect to incur most of these charges in the second quarter of 2026.</span></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On April&#160;10, 2026, our manufacturing facility in Bedford Park, Illinois experienced a thermal event in our corn germ processing operations (&#8220;Argo thermal event&#8221;). As a result of the Argo thermal event, we expect to incur direct costs of approximately $20 million primarily related to inventory write-downs and machinery repairs, which we expect to recognize in the second quarter of 2026. </span></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We evaluated the Argo thermal event as a subsequent event and estimated direct costs disclosed above as of May&#160;8, 2026. We continue to diagnose circumstances related to the event, and estimates and actual amounts may change as our evaluations progress, costs are incurred, and expenditures are realized.</span></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Supply Chain Finance Programs</span></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Under supply chain finance programs administered by third-party banks, our suppliers have the opportunity to sell receivables due from us to participating financing institutions and receive earlier payment at a discount. Our responsibility is limited to making payment on the terms originally negotiated with our supplier, regardless of whether such supplier sells its receivable to a financial institution. The payment terms we negotiate with a supplier are independent of whether such </span></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">supplier participates in a supply chain finance program, and participation in any such program by a supplier has no effect on our income or cash flows.</span></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As of March&#160;31, 2026 and December&#160;31, 2025, participating financial institutions held $131 million and $148 million of our liabilities recorded in Accounts payable and Accrued liabilities and liabilities held for sale on our Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets. As of March&#160;31, 2026, supply chain finance programs existed primarily for operations in Brazil, Thailand, the U.S., China, Mexico, certain PureCircle entities</span><span style="color:#242424;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">, Colombia and Peru.</span></div><span></span>
